evidence: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17-31 never checks req.method. Sibling handlers do enforce it, e.g. apps/web/pages/api/cron/syncAppMeta.ts:24 and apps/web/pages/api/auth/signup.ts:19 return 405. Impact is small because the secret check still gates access and a non-POST request has no body, so zod parsing fails anyway.

app-credential.ts:25 indexes req.headers with the raw value of process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME. Node lowercases incoming header names, so a value like 'X-Calcom-Secret' always looks up undefined and every request gets a 403. It fails closed rather than open, but the configurable header is unusable unless it is lowercase. Fix: call .toLowerCase() on the name.

app-credential.ts:24-28 uses strict !==. If the value were an array, array !== string is true, so the request gets a 403; it is not allowed through. Node also joins repeated custom headers into a single ', '-separated string, which likewise fails the comparison. Both cases fail closed.

app-credential.ts:31 calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) with no try/catch. A ZodError escapes the handler and Next.js returns a 500 for bad input. Use safeParse and return a 400.

app-credential.ts:57-59 runs JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) with no error handling, and the key falls back to an empty string. A bad ciphertext, wrong key or bad JSON throws, which becomes a 500 instead of a 400.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-11: ZodType does not override toString, so both computed keys become the literal '[object Object]'. The second key (z.unknown().optional()) overwrites the first in the object literal, so the key is NOT required and payloads with access_token pass. The real bug is different: zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so expires_in, expiry_date and refresh_token are dropped from .data, leaving only access_token (plus the refresh_token placeholder). The schema is broken, but not for the reason given. Fix: z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough() or a catchall.

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26-28 sets data.refresh_token = 'refresh_token' when it is missing. office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264-265 spreads tokenResponse.data over the stored credentials, so the real refresh token is overwritten with the placeholder and saved at :266-273. In the sync path refresh_token is always missing because the schema strips it (see #5). In the non-sync path refreshTokenResponseSchema has refresh_token optional (office365calendar CalendarService.ts:56). Later provider refreshes then fail.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 returns a raw fetch Response in the sync branch. Callers that expect another shape break: googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-94 reads res?.data (undefined on a Response, so token.access_token throws). zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:85-96 and zohocrm CalendarService.ts:204-217 read .data.error. hubspot CalendarService.ts:177 treats it as a HubspotToken object. Fetch-based callers (office365, webex, zoom, lark) work.

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15: a rejected fetch propagates to the caller exactly as the original provider fetch/axios calls did before this PR (e.g. zoom/office365 refreshAccessToken had no try/catch around fetch either). Behaviour is unchanged, and the callers' existing error paths (e.g. the try/catch in googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:84) apply.

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 fetch has no AbortSignal/timeout. That is true, but none of the pre-existing provider refresh fetches in this repo set one either (e.g. zoomvideo VideoApiAdapter.ts:79-92, webex VideoApiAdapter.ts:62-78). It is a hardening improvement, not a regression.

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 types the callback as () => any and has no return type, so the result is any. This is why the Response vs AxiosResponse/HubspotToken mismatch in #7/#14 compiles silently. A generic signature <T>(fn: () => Promise<T>) => Promise<T | Response> would surface those bugs.

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 does not check response.ok. For fetch-based callers, status is already checked downstream by handleErrorsJson (office365calendar CalendarService.ts:263), handleZoomResponse, handleWebexResponse and handleLarkError. The real breakage for axios/Google/Hubspot callers is the shape mismatch (#7), not missing validation.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 calls prisma.credential.update, but the imports (lines 1-20) have no prisma import (grep finds only line 96). This gives a TS error and a runtime ReferenceError in getClient.

zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:69 refreshAccessToken(credentialId, ...) passes credentialId (credential.id, see :62) as the userId argument of refreshOAuthTokens at :85-94. The sync endpoint gets calcomUserId set to a credential id, so it targets the wrong user. userId needs to be threaded through.

zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:204-217 reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error and .data.expiryDate. With sync enabled, refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 returns a fetch Response, whose .data is undefined, so .data.error throws a TypeError. Same root cause as #7.

app-credential.ts:62-92 does findFirst then create. packages/prisma/schema.prisma:127-146 Credential has only @@index([userId]) and @@index([appId]), with no unique constraint on (userId, appId), so two concurrent webhook calls for the same user and app can both create. The race is real but unlikely for a server-to-server sync webhook, and the codebase generally allows multiple credentials per app.

office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 now calls parseRefreshTokenResponse, which throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' when parsing fails (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:22-24). The prisma.credential.update at :266 is never reached. That is the opposite of silently persisting. (The removed console.error was the old behaviour.)

salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-104 fetches and stores new tokens (accessTokenParsed.data) but builds jsforce.Connection with credentialKey.instance_url and credentialKey.access_token, the stale values from the original credential. The refreshed access_token is never used in this connection.

googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 sets key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...), which returns the SafeParse result {success, data} (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:30). :98-101 then persists that wrapper as credential.key. The next load's googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) at :75 fails, corrupting the credential. Should use .data.
